summary.prose: Links in assistant replies and in review-pane documents become clickable. http and https links open in the browser, and a repository file path with an optional line, such as src/foo.ts:42, becomes a link that opens that file at that line in the editor. The page only reports what was clicked; the extension host validates the target and does the opening, so the strict CSP and the guardMd scrub stay as they are.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Make links and code references clickable in the chat and the review pane

api.name: guardMd

parameters.name: el
parameters.purpose: the rendered markdown container to scrub and linkify

returns.meaning: the container is scrubbed as today (non-http(s) hrefs dropped); afterwards code references in text outside code, pre and anchors, and inline code elements (not under pre) whose whole text is a code reference, are wrapped in anchors carrying data-path and data-line, and http(s) anchors lose their href and keep only data-url, so VS Code's own link handling has nothing to open and the click handler is the single path

errors.condition: any failure inside the scrub is caught, as today, and leaves the rendered text unlinked

preconditions: el holds the output of marked.parse
postconditions: every http(s) anchor carries data-url and every code reference carries data-path
text inside pre elements and inside inline code that is not wholly a code reference is never wrapped

api.name: open-attachment
api.signature: { type: 'open-link'; url: string } | { type: 'open-code-ref'; path: string; line?: number | undefined }

parameters.name: url
parameters.purpose: the clicked http or https address

returns.meaning: two new page-to-host messages added beside open-attachment and open-companion in protocol.ts and its allowlist. The file opens in the column chosen by chooseReviewColumn (review-column.ts), the same rule that places the review pane

errors.condition: the host drops a url that is not http or https, and a path that is absolute, contains .. segments, resolves outside the workspace folder, or does not exist; each is logged, never thrown

preconditions: sent by the delegated click handler after preventDefault
postconditions: a valid url opens in the browser; a valid path opens in the editor with the line selected, in the editor group the review pane placement chooses (an existing group that holds no chat tab, else the active group), never in the chat group

dataModelChanges.details: Two new message variants, open-link and open-code-ref, added to the webview-to-host union and its allowlist. No stored data changes. The hosts receive their open dependencies from extension.ts, since chat-panel.ts and docs-review-panel.ts do not import vscode; the vscode.d.ts shim gains env.openExternal, Range and Position. On the chat surface the linkify step and the guardMd href change land in render-registry.ts, keeping the innerHTML-then-guardMd pairing that render-registry.test.ts asserts. Existing tests that pin the old scrub change with it: docs-review-panel.test.ts t4 (guardMd strips a non-http href and an image src) asserts that an https href survives with rel and target, and is rewritten to assert no href, a data-url and the same non-http and image scrub; its stub DOM is extended so the linkify step can run. render-registry.test.ts string assertions on guardMd are checked and updated the same way. The review-pane shell is pinned byte-for-byte: the SHELL_BASELINE chars, bytes and sha256 constants (the t1 shell-baseline test and its matching pin) are updated in the same commit that changes the shell, and the linkify fragment is inlined once into the review shell (inside the renderer source), so the 'inlines each source string verbatim and exactly once' test keeps holding. Clicked files are placed by the existing chooseReviewColumn rule; that function is reused as is, not changed.

migration.stateBefore: Chat and review-pane markdown is rendered by marked and scrubbed by guardMd. guardMd keeps http(s) hrefs and sets rel=noopener noreferrer and target=_blank on them, so VS Code's own webview link handling may already open them; it drops every other href (removing the href but leaving the anchor), and no click handler of ours exists (render-registry.ts and docs-review-panel.ts, from the s1 bundles).
migration.stateAfter: http(s) links and repository file references are clickable on both surfaces. guardMd strips the href from handled anchors and keeps the target in a data attribute, so VS Code's own link handling has nothing to open; one delegated click handler posts open-link or open-code-ref and the host validates and opens the target. The CSP is unchanged and guardMd still never leaves a non-http(s) href.

migrationSteps.action: Add the open-link and open-code-ref message variants and allowlist entries to the protocol

Add the host handlers to the chat host and the review-pane host: open-link opens an http(s) url externally, open-code-ref validates the path with a new exported helper (resolveWithin(root, relPath, fs) returning the real path or undefined) extracted from companion-reader.ts; createCompanionReader is rewired onto it unchanged (docs/ root, .html, size cap) and its existing tests stay green; the host then opens the path at the line. Inject the open-external and open-file-at-line dependencies and the workspace folder from extension.ts into both hosts, and add env.openExternal, Range and Position to the vscode.d.ts shim so a real Range selects the line. The open-file-at-line dependency in extension.ts takes its viewColumn from the existing reviewColumn closure (chooseReviewColumn over the tab groups), so a clicked code reference opens in the same group the review pane would; if the closure yields no column the file opens Beside, as the quiet review pane does, so it never lands in the chat group

Extend the page scripts of both surfaces with the linkify step after guardMd, a rule that styles the handled anchors as links, and the delegated click handler, updating the review-pane SHELL_BASELINE pins in the same commit

migration.backwardCompat: Additive: no stored data, no existing message changes meaning; an older page that does not send the new messages is unaffected.

alternativesConsidered.name: Page-side linkify + host-side validated open
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: After marked + guardMd, the page script wraps code references in links and one delegated click handler posts the target to the host, which validates and opens it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A shared page-script fragment (used by both render-registry.ts and docs-review-panel.ts) runs after guardMd: it walks text nodes outside code/pre/a, wraps path[:line[-line]] matches in anchors carrying data attributes, and keeps http(s) hrefs. A single delegated click listener on the container preventDefaults and posts {type:'open-link', url} or {type:'open-code-ref', path, line}. The host validates (http/https only for url; path resolved under the workspace folder, must exist, no escape) and opens via vscode.env.openExternal or vscode.open with a selection.
pros: Reuses the existing guardMd pipeline and the open-attachment message pattern
Host is the only place that opens anything; CSP unchanged
cons: Recognition runs in the page, so it is testable only via the stub-DOM harness
Text-node walking must be careful around code blocks and existing links

alternativesConsidered.name: Pure recognizer module + host resolves
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A pure TS recognizer is inlined into the page script by stringification; host does the same validated open.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Write the code-reference recognizer as a pure function in its own module (unit-testable), embed its source into the page script via Function.prototype.toString, and use the same delegated click + host open-link/open-code-ref messages as a1.
pros: Recognition rules unit-tested directly in Node
Same safe host-side open as a1
cons: Stringifying a function into the page is fragile under tsx/tsc output
Extra indirection for a small rule set
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same runtime behaviour as a1 with better unit-testability, but function stringification is fragile and adds indirection for a small rule set.

alternativesConsidered.name: Host-side rewrite before render
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The host rewrites markdown to add links before it reaches the page.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The host preprocesses assistant markdown, replacing code references with markdown links using a custom scheme, and guardMd is widened to allow that scheme; clicks post the scheme target back.
pros: Recognition runs in Node and is simple to test
cons: Streaming responses render incrementally in the page, so host rewriting does not cover them
Widens guardMd to a new scheme, weakening the scrub
Review pane documents are rendered in the page too
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Does not cover streamed rendering and requires weakening guardMd.
